title: Stacks, queues and deques
summary: Last-in-first-out, first-in-first-out, and the problems each one fits.

questions.prompt: Check whether a string of brackets like "([]{})" is balanced, with three kinds of bracket. Which approach?
options: Push opening brackets on a stack; each closing bracket must match the top
Put the brackets in a queue

questions.prompt: Why is ArrayDeque preferred over the old Stack class in modern Java?
options: Stack is a legacy, synchronized class built on Vector; ArrayDeque is the recommended, faster choice

questions.prompt: Put the steps of a balanced-brackets check in order.
steps: If the stack is empty at the end, the brackets are balanced
For each character, push it if it's an opening bracket
For a closing bracket, pop and check it matches; fail if the stack was empty or it doesn't match

questions.prompt: This finds the next greater element for every position. What is its time complexity for an array of length n?
True or false: a queue's next removed element is the one added most recently.
